0: Be quick! I see her there, returning.
7:
Go! go! I never will retreat.

Here is a casket, not unmeet, Which elsewhere I have just been earning. Here, set it in the press, with haste! I swear, ’twill turn her head, to spy it: Some baubles I therein had placed, That you might win another by it. True, child is child, and play is play.
11:
I know not, should I do it?

Ask you, pray? Yourself, perhaps, would keep the bubble? Then I suggest, ’twere fair and just To spare the lovely day your lust, And spare to me the further trouble. You are not miserly, I trust? I rub my hands, in expectation tender—
18: (He places the casket in the press, and locks it again.)
24: Now quick, away! The sweet young maiden to betray, So that by wish and will you bend her; And you look as though To the lecture-hall you were forced to go,— As if stood before you, gray and loath, Physics and Metaphysics both! But away! [Exeunt.
33: It is so close, so sultry, here!
35: And yet ’tis not so warm outside. I feel, I know not why, such fear!— Would mother came!—where can she bide? My body’s chill and shuddering,— I’m but a silly, fearsome thing!
44: There was a King in Thule, Was faithful till the grave,— To whom his mistress, dying, A golden goblet gave.
50: Naught was to him more precious; He drained it at every bout: His eyes with tears ran over, As oft as he drank thereout.
56: When came his time of dying, The towns in his land he told, Naught else to his heir denying Except the goblet of gold.
62: He sat at the royal banquet With his knights of high degree, In the lofty hall of his fathers In the Castle by the Sea.
68: There stood the old carouser, And drank the last life-glow; And hurled the hallowed goblet Into the tide below.
74: He saw it plunging and filling, And sinking deep in the sea: Then fell his eyelids forever, And never more drank he!
80:
(She opens the press in order to arrange her clothes, and perceives the casket of jewels.)

How comes that lovely casket here to me? I locked the press, most certainly. ’Tis truly wonderful! What can within it be? Perhaps ’twas brought by some one as a pawn, And mother gave a loan thereon? And here there hangs a key to fit: I have a mind to open it. What is that? God in Heaven! Whence came Such things? Never beheld I aught so fair! Rich ornaments, such as a noble dame On highest holidays might wear! How would the pearl-chain suit my hair? Ah, who may all this splendor own?
85:
(She adorns herself with the jewelry, and steps before the mirror.)

Were but the ear-rings mine, alone! One has at once another air. What helps one’s beauty, youthful blood? One may possess them, well and good; But none the more do others care. They praise us half in pity, sure: To gold still tends, On gold depends All, all! Alas, we poor!
93: (FAUST, walking thoughtfully up and down. To him MEPHISTOPHELES.)
101: By all love ever rejected! By hell-fire hot and unsparing! I wish I knew something worse, that I might use it for swearing!
108: What ails thee? What is’t gripes thee, elf? A face like thine beheld I never.
116: I would myself unto the Devil deliver, If I were not a Devil myself!
123:
Thy head is out of order, sadly: It much becomes thee to be raving madly.

Just think, the pocket of a priest should get The trinkets left for Margaret! The mother saw them, and, instanter, A secret dread began to haunt her. Keen scent has she for tainted air; She snuffs within her book of prayer, And smells each article, to see If sacred or profane it be; So here she guessed, from every gem, That not much blessing came with them. “My child,” she said, “ill-gotten good Ensnares the soul, consumes the blood. Before the Mother of God we’ll lay it; With heavenly manna she’ll repay it!” But Margaret thought, with sour grimace, “A gift-horse is not out of place, And, truly! godless cannot be The one who brought such things to me.” A parson came, by the mother bidden: He saw, at once, where the game was hidden, And viewed it with a favor stealthy. He spake: “That is the proper view,— Who overcometh, winneth too. The Holy Church has a stomach healthy: Hath eaten many a land as forfeit, And never yet complained of surfeit: The Church alone, beyond all question, Has for ill-gotten goods the right digestion.”
132:
A general practice is the same, Which Jew and King may also claim.

Then bagged the spangles, chains, and rings, As if but toadstools were the things, And thanked no less, and thanked no more Than if a sack of nuts he bore,— Promised them fullest heavenly pay, And deeply edified were they.
143: Sits unrestful still, And knows not what she should, or will; Thinks on the jewels, day and night, But more on him who gave her such delight.
150: The darling’s sorrow gives me pain. Get thou a set for her again! The first was not a great display.
157: O yes, the gentleman finds it all child’s-play!
164: Fix and arrange it to my will; And on her neighbor try thy skill! Don’t be a Devil stiff as paste, But get fresh jewels to her taste!
171: Yes, gracious Sir, in all obedience!
175: Such an enamored fool in air would blow Sun, moon, and all the starry legions, To give his sweetheart a diverting show.
184: God forgive my husband, yet he Hasn’t done his duty by me! Off in the world he went straightway,— Left me lie in the straw where I lay. And, truly, I did naught to fret him: God knows I loved, and can’t forget him!
193: Perhaps he’s even dead! Ah, woe!— Had I a certificate to show!
210: I scarce can stand, my knees are trembling! I find a box, the first resembling, Within my press! Of ebony,— And things, all splendid to behold, And richer far than were the old.
217: You mustn’t tell it to your mother! ’Twould go to the priest, as did the other.
223: Ah, look and see—just look and see!
231: O, what a blessed luck for thee!
236:
But, ah! in the streets I dare not bear them, Nor in the church be seen to wear them.

Yet thou canst often this way wander, And secretly the jewels don, Walk up and down an hour, before the mirror yonder,— We’ll have our private joy thereon. And then a chance will come, a holiday, When, piece by piece, can one the things abroad display, A chain at first, then other ornament: Thy mother will not see, and stories we’ll invent.
244: Whoever could have brought me things so precious? That something’s wrong, I feel suspicious.
251: Good Heaven! My mother can that have been?
259: That I so boldly introduce me, I beg you, ladies, to excuse me.
271: I’m she: what does the gentleman desire?
275: It is enough that you are she: You’ve a visitor of high degree. Pardon the freedom I have ta’en,— Will after noon return again.
282: Of all things in the world! Just hear— He takes thee for a lady, dear!
289: I am a creature young and poor: The gentleman’s too kind, I’m sure. The jewels don’t belong to me.
296: Ah, not alone the jewelry! The look, the manner, both betray— Rejoiced am I that I may stay!
304: What is your business? I would fain—
308: I would I had a more cheerful strain! Take not unkindly its repeating: Your husband’s dead, and sends a greeting.
315: Is dead? Alas, that heart so true! My husband dead! Let me die, too!
320: Ah, dearest dame, let not your courage fail!
328: Hear me relate the mournful tale!
334: Therefore I’d never love, believe me! A loss like this to death would grieve me.
341: Joy follows woe, woe after joy comes flying.
344: Relate his life’s sad close to me!
347: In Padua buried, he is lying Beside the good Saint Antony, Within a grave well consecrated, For cool, eternal rest created.
354: He gave you, further, no commission?
361: Yes, one of weight, with many sighs: Three hundred masses buy, to save him from perdition! My hands are empty, otherwise.
368: What! Not a pocket-piece? no jewelry? What every journeyman within his wallet spares, And as a token with him bears, And rather starves or begs, than loses?
375: Madam, it is a grief to me; Yet, on my word, his cash was put to proper uses. Besides, his penitence was very sore, And he lamented his ill fortune all the more.
382: Alack, that men are so unfortunate! Surely for his soul’s sake full many a prayer I’ll proffer.
396: You well deserve a speedy marriage-offer: You are so kind, compassionate.
404: O, no! As yet, it would not do.
